title: I Enforced the Badminton Court Clock on the Duo Who Booked a Ghost Hour

parts.text: I booked court 3 at 7:00 p.m. and a duo was already playing under a reservation name that was not in the kiosk. The clock policy said: BOOK ONLINE. CLOCK STARTS. GHOST NAMES DROP. I was thirty-two, rec member, holding a kiosk print. Duo lead Nina did not leave. "Ghosts are warmups." I photographed the empty kiosk name, the print, and their shuttle tube on my hour. Then I logged a ghost. At 7:08 the gym desk asked why Nina's tube was on a name that did not exist. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The gym desk can see Nina's shuttle tube on court 3 under a kiosk name that is blank.

social.video_title: They played my hour under a ghost booking name — Part 1/2
social.description: Badminton, a kiosk print, and a duo on my court. I logged the ghost. Would you have shown the clock?

parts.text: Nina called it leftover until the desk asked for the log. I printed the ghost, the photo, and the print. They dropped. Nina booked a real hour and told the gym leftovers were always about optics. Optics is a word duos use when a tube exists. Clock policy now has a second line: GHOSTS DROP. I keep my hour. Nina books. The court finally looks like a clock, not a rumor. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Ghost log, open court, and a second line. Was leftover ever a blank kiosk?
